name: Trish Scarborough: I Spy a Seeker | Chapter 2 Core Only
description_md:
I Spy a Seeker

`These are replacement decks for Chapter 2 investigators. All have been playtested in Chapter 2, and also extensively in Chapter 1. If you want to support my work, give it a like ❤︎ and a favorite ★ on here!` >It's Chapter 2 time! Here [Trish](/card/12007) boasts strong enemy management, with 5 and the [M1903 Hammerless](/card/12045), but also the ability to investigate at a 6 or 7 stat. What more could you ask for in a Seeker... Rogue, I mean Rogue! NOTE: There is an error where decks containing newer versions of cards cannot be posted currently (e.g. [Overpower](/card/01091) vs. [Overpower](/card/12092)). I won't be able to change the deck retrospectively to the new Ch2 cards, so please click this link for a version of the deck with the Chapter 2 cards.

Series Decks

|   Seeker   |   Survivor   |   Guardian   |    Rogue   |   Mystic   | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Joe | Izzie | Daniela| Trish | Dexter |

At a Glance

>| Stats | | >|:---|:---| >| Clue-finding: |  ★★★★★ | >| Consistency: |  ★★★★☆ | >| Enemy Management: |  ★★★★☆ | >| Encounter Defense: |  ★★☆☆☆ | >| Survivability: |  ★★★☆☆ | >| Simplicity: |  ★★★★☆ | I thought I'd implement a [Valentin](https://arkhamdb.com/user/profile/42890/Valentin1331)-style rating system to make these guides more accessible. "Consistency" covers card draw and resource economy. In essence it's an outcome measure of "does the resource economy cover the costs of my asset engine and desirable events, and can I find my engine and play it?"

Overview

- Green Seeker is best Seeker: With two [Magnifying Glasses](/card/12034) and [Dorothy Simmons](/card/12030), Trish investigates at a 7 (or a 6 with [Hammerless](/card/12045)). There's 19 icons in this deck to commit to tests, as well as [Breaking and Entering](/card/12050) for a big boost, and [Deduction](/card/12039) plus [Working a Hunch](/card/12038) for extra clues. Trish's extra evade has the knock-on effect of often giving her more free actions to investigate - high intellect is good to capitalize on that. - The spy who... shot me: This deck is rich enough to afford [Olivier](/card/12046), who you can be played with [Dorothy](/card/12030) due to [Charisma](/card/12095). Olivier gives you a +1 boost, ideal for shooting [Black Chamber Operative](/card/12009) with [Hammerless](/card/12045) or for general evading. The art thief's ability to move away from an enemy you just evaded or drag enemies around prior to evading is top notch. [Out of Sight](/card/12057), [Through the Cracks](/card/12041) and an over-success on [Breaking and Entering](/card/12050) provide further enemy management options. - Mo' money, mo' mentum: [Another Day, Another Dollar](/card/12056) provides free resources that don't eat actions. When you throw in [Magnifying Glass](/card/12034) and [Prestidigitation](/card/12052), what at first looks like a large and expensive engine isn't anywhere near as bad in practice. With an idealized opening hand of [Dorothy](/card/12030), [Olivier](/card/12046), Magnifying Glass, Prestidigitation and [Lucky Cigarette Case](/card/12044) you can play *all of these* and still have Olivier's move and one action to spare. Even with a worse hand, setup is never disappointing. - Card draw and free movement: Card draw is [Lucky Cigarette Case](/card/12044) and [Covert Ops](/card/12008), with [Perception](/card/12093) and [Manual Dexterity](/card/12091). Try and get LCC into play early if you can, as card draw dries up otherwise. Alternatively Covert Ops can provide a move action, with Olivier adding another. Further move (and disengage) actions come from [Through the Cracks](/card/12041) evading and [Out of Sight](/card/12057), as well as your ability (you don't need to succeed to trigger it). - Encounter management: With this deck having robust enemy management and clue-finding, the drawback is it's pressed for space. As such there's a modest 4 and 7 icons in the deck, which are your defense against willpower treacheries. [Dorothy](/card/12030) and [Olivier](/card/12046) are soak, kill them off when you need to - on occasion you can pay for a second copy. Thank you: [5argon](https://arkhamdb.com/user/profile/61394/5argon) and [their thumbnail tool](https://arkham-starter.com/tool/thumbnails); [Valentin1331](https://arkhamdb.com/user/profile/42890/Valentin1331) for his support over the years; the community creators of [ArkhamDB](https://www.patreon.com/c/kamalisk/) ([kamalisk](https://www.reddit.com/user/kamalisk/)), [Arkham.Build](https://www.patreon.com/c/arkhambuild/) ([Felix](https://spoettel.dev/)) and [Arkham Cards](https://www.patreon.com/c/arkhamcards/) ([zzorba](https://www.reddit.com/user/zzorba/)) - linking their Patreons!

Explain Yourself!

I always knew I wanted [Dorothy](/card/12030) in this deck, as her card compression is just too good (she's a stat booster, a resource engine and emergency soak all rolled into one). The decision point is therefore whether to take [Olivier](/card/12046) and [Charisma](/card/12095). [Another Day, Another Dollar](/card/12056) plus [Dorothy](/card/12030) and [Emergency Cache](/card/12089) mean you can comfortably afford [Olivier](/card/12046), and his move refunds the action you take to play him. As such, while he's expensive and another asset to play, I think the benefits overwhelmingly outweigh the costs. In terms of what isn't here, no [Thieves' Kit](/card/12049) or [Sticky Fingers](/card/12054) as you make enough money anyway. I wasn't keen on [Mysterious Grimoire](/card/12040), as hand slots are hotly contested and it can pull [Black Chamber Operative](/card/12009). [Gather Intel](/card/12036) or [Guts](/card/12090) would be nice, but there just isn't space. With [Fingerprint Kit](/card/12031) it's very expensive and, with [Hammerless](/card/12045) already in the deck, again I didn't want hand slot competition. [Sharp Rhetoric](/card/12035) is an alright idea, but boosting is pricey and you can use the resource saving to replay [Olivier](/card/12046) or [Dorothy](/card/12030). New starter deck additions: As free horror healing for what you want to be doing already, Unflappable is a straight swap for [Through the Cracks](/card/12041). Deduction •• is an obvious choice and I'd upgrade into it early. I'd swap [Manual Dexterity](/card/12091) for Out the Door (and later the upgraded version), and [Emergency Cache](/card/12089) for "Watch this!". [Breaking and Entering](/card/12050) becomes Caustic Reaction to help tackle [Black Chamber Operative](/card/12009) (as now upgraded Deduction supports big investigate actions, so B&E isn't as needed). I would swap [Unexpected Courage](/card/12094) for Quick Exit and then also upgrade Quick Exit. This deck then has horror healing and more icons for events, with some splashy resource skills on top and a little more enemy management. Upgraded Caustic Reaction is probably your luxury upgrade here.

Campaign starter and planned progression

0 XP deck is below (and link here). A recommended order of purchases/upgrades is: - 1 x [Another Day, Another Dollar](/card/12056) - 1 x [Charisma](/card/12095) - 1 x [Another Day, Another Dollar](/card/12056) - [Through the Cracks](/card/12037) → [Through the Cracks ••](/card/12041) - [Out of Sight](/card/12053) → [Out of Sight •••](/card/12057) The fully upgraded deck and starter deck play very similarly, with [Charisma](/card/12095) allowing you to run both [Olivier](/card/12046) and [Dorothy](/card/12030) and [Another Day, Another Dollar](/card/12056) easing setup. [Through the Cracks](/card/12041) is a lot nicer when upgraded, which is why it's picked before [Out of Sight](/card/12057).

Final thoughts

This deck is absurdly good! [Olivier](/card/12046) and Trish mean if feels like you have 4 or 5 actions most turns, and then your is strong enough to hoover up clues at pace. The big downside is [Black Chamber Operative](/card/12009), so pairing Trish with someone who can help deal with him is wise. Even so, this deck does an alright job of managing him solo. If [Skids](/card/01003) was considered one of the weakest investigators of the old core, then I'd say Trish here is easily the strongest. Hope you like the deck and give it a try! May the [Black Chamber Operative](/card/12009) be forever at the bottom of your deck...
